sources.measurement_method: Filtered 7,529 non-ground returns inside the OSM TREC ring and compared them with 12,968 class-2 ground returns in a 60 ft surrounding window. Across-width 12-bin medians rise from 9.693 m and 9.665 m in the outer bins to a 14.373 m central-bin maximum; values are relative to the surrounding class-2 ground median of 619.28 ft. Because roof returns are class 1/unclassified and ground uses a nearby median, the modeled 9.7 m eave and 14.4 m ridge are LiDAR-derived estimates, not surveyed heights.
sources.uncertainty: No class-6 building returns occur inside either footprint. Outermost bins include non-roof/ground returns, and nearby ground varies p05-p95 from 617.98-620.78 ft. Quantile-based profile provides a roof-height envelope, not exact eave or ridge survey measurements.

footprint_source_comparison.note: The prior manifest bounds match the 2021 OSM way bounds exactly, while current Purdue GIS OID 312 is about 2.376 m west, 0.443 m south, and 1.212 m narrower east-west. The orthophoto shows both outlines on the same TREC roof: OSM tracks the visible roof edge more closely on the east side, while Purdue GIS is displaced west and extends beyond the visible roof on portions of the west side. This is not explained by a simple uniform roof-overhang offset; no source establishes which perimeter is the structural wall line. The rebuild retains the named current Purdue GIS polygon as the primary wall footprint, keeps the OSM outline as an explicit roof-edge alternative, and reports the position conflict for coordinator review. Ring areas are close, but four area measures differ: computed GIS ring about 34,124 sq ft, GIS squarefootage attribute 36,210 sq ft, Purdue Treasurer Oct 2021 building-list area 36,545.51 sq ft, and RecWell project-size figure 29,037 sq ft. Their definitions/scopes are unresolved.

orthophoto_observation.visual_result: Both footprints lie over the same long north-south light-roofed field hall in the orthophoto. Purdue GIS OID 312 is shifted about 2.4 m west and 0.44 m south from the 2021 OSM outline, and is about 1.21 m narrower east-west; red/blue separation is visible along the perimeter and does not alter facility identity.

orthophoto_observation.roof_observation: Orthophoto shows a long north-south roof ridge, two sloped planes and repeated light-colored east-west bands perpendicular to the ridge. The roof appears white/light gray. Roof heights are not measurable from this orthographic image.

vertical_geometry.basis: 2018 Indiana QL2 LiDAR return profile inside the OSM roof ring compared with nearby classified ground. Outer-bin medians are 9.693 m and 9.665 m; central-bin median reaches 14.373 m. These support approximate 9.7 m eave and 14.4 m ridge values but do not measure a surveyed wall/eave plane because roof returns are unclassified and ground is sampled nearby.

lidar_sample.measurement_status: LiDAR-derived roof-profile estimate; not surveyed building heights

design_decisions_and_uncertainty: Purdue RecWell identifies a dedicated indoor synthetic turf field, and the official GIS identifies the separate TREC building at 1252 Third Street. The model therefore depicts one long clear-span field hall rather than the adjacent multistory CoRec or Aquatic Center.

The RecWell fact sheet identifies TREC as 29,037 sq ft (25,929 sq ft turf, 2,554 sq ft locker rooms, 554 sq ft office/control), and the facility page states a 60 yd x 40 yd indoor artificial turf field. These establish use and program areas, but do not provide exterior height or room placement.

The 2023 orthophoto confirms a long north-south ridge, two roof planes, a pale roof and repeated east-west bands perpendicular to the ridge. It does not reveal roof height. The model uses this observed roof plan and transverse seam rhythm on a light-gray roof surface.

The AIA Columbus album and Moody Nolan page cover the larger France A. Cordova CoRec expansion/renovation, not a specifically identified TREC facade. Their imagery and design descriptions are excluded from TREC geometry/material claims.

Purdue RecWell accessibility text places the at-grade TREC entry on the circle drive west of CoRec. The July 2023 TREC-specific Street View panorama shows a glazed entry at the northeast/east corner on that approach. The model adds the observed corner glazing and canopy; exact bay, dimensions and glazing grid are estimated from perspective.

2018 QL2 LiDAR supports a roof profile of roughly 9.7 m at the eaves and 14.4 m at the ridge above nearby ground. These are estimates rather than surveyed building dimensions; no published TREC section or elevation was found.

The red Purdue GIS ring is shifted relative to the blue OSM ring and neither one yields a consistent symmetric roof-overhang interpretation against the orthophoto. The modeled walls retain the official named GIS ring; roof-overhang and exact wall-to-roof relationship remain unresolved.

Purdue Archives accession 2026-186 is an unprocessed 4.07 GB/661-file digital folder whose inventory lists TREC among photographed buildings. However, no TREC-specific filenames, captions, thumbnails, or item-level links are exposed; the accession page returned HTTP 403. The Historic Database TREC record 165 has image_url=null and images=[]. The accession confirms that photographs exist at collection level, but no visible photo can be attributed to a TREC exterior or entrance, so no facade geometry or material is inferred. See the accession search-index extract and access-record JSON in the sources folder.

All three official Purdue Athletics TREC-linked photos were opened directly. They are interior field views showing artificial turf and overhead metal roof framing; no exterior is visible, so they do not support facade details.

A Google Maps Street View panorama labeled from the official TREC place listing provides TREC-specific exterior pixels. Metadata: panorama CKWL7p3cJEsDPH5hReovcw, capture date July 2023, camera at 40.428913,-86.9239926, yaw 206.01 degrees. The east/northeast-facing view shows red-brown brick base, light vertically ribbed metal above, a glazed corner entry and projecting canopy, one visible window, service doors and wall louvers. The model uses these observed facade types; stationing, heights and dimensions are approximate. Only the viewed side is supported; unseen facades remain unverified. See the updated Google Street View access/inspection record in sources.
